fields.description:
Replacement/residual bug split from witted-invisible-roan after completion verification refused close on 2026-09-07.

Residual defect:
The configured rebar MCP endpoint can still return persistent HTTP 502 after concurrent gate load if the MCP process is OOM-killed or otherwise dies while nginx's materialized single-server upstream still points at the dead backend. The parent landed detection, retire-sweep repair, memory instrumentation, and a reduced whole-store read footprint, but those do not prove the serving path cannot recur under concurrent gate load.

Verifier blocker on parent, summarized:
- nginx still has a single materialized upstream with no failover path;
- memory oversubscription under concurrent gates is not bounded by admission control, instance sizing, or off-box execution;
- existing comments identify the latency/read-scan issue (`lousy-unsuited-gnu` / `94c5-b42e-ac80-4f06`) as separate and not fixed by the memory reduction.

Design question to resolve here:
Choose the prevention mechanism(s) for recurrence — e.g. MCP upstream failover/self-healing, gate admission/concurrency limits, moving gate execution off-box, or a data-backed capacity change — and implement enough that `/mcp` cannot remain pinned to a dead backend after gate-induced MCP failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The selected design is recorded with why alternatives were accepted/rejected.
- [ ] A reproduced or simulated MCP backend death under gate-like load recovers without a persistent nginx 502.
- [ ] The prevention is covered by tests through the relevant surface(s) and by an operator-visible metric/log/alarm.
- [ ] Any capacity/concurrency number used by the prevention cites measured data, including or linking the AC5 campaign split to `inherited-americium-porpoise`.


## RCA / design decision (2026-09-07)

Phase 1 facts from the paired tickets and host incident work:

- `enduring-ironclad-arrowana` removed the largest measured long-lived review-time memory
  multiplier: `PlanRelationSnapshot.ticket_states_by_id` retained 256,646,460 bytes on a
  9,081-ticket store before the fix and 37,046 bytes after, while preserving review inputs.
  Its Gerrit change 2807 is submitted; this ticket builds on that load-side reduction rather
  than duplicating it.
- Parent `witted-invisible-roan` already changed the MCP retire sweep to retain a crashed live
  backend instead of `docker rm`-ing it while nginx still points at the port. That avoids making
  a transient exit unrestartable, but it still leaves `/mcp` pinned to a dead port until Docker
  restart or a human/source-changing deploy recovers it.
- On the P1 Gerrit-object incident, current host pressure was not acute (root 32%, data 24%,
  gate-scratch 29%) but BuildKit had been in ALARM from a 95% cap reading. This supports a
  conservative recovery path that does not add a second MCP container during memory pressure.

Selected prevention: in-place live-backend restart on every autodeploy tick. If the nginx
upstream port belongs to a managed MCP container and that container is not running, autodeploy
must run a bounded self-heal branch before source-change deploy decisions:

1. emit a countable `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker with reason `mcp-live-backend-down` (existing
   observability path; no new HCL required);
2. run `docker start <live-container>` (not `rm -f`, not a second blue/green container), so the
   existing container name and host port stay aligned with nginx's single-server upstream;
3. require the same `/health`, store-readiness, and startup-handshake readiness contract used for
   normal MCP promotion;
4. emit `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL` on success as a journal/log evidence marker, clear MCP backoff,
   and leave nginx untouched because the port did not change;
5. on failed start/readiness, keep the upstream and container identity intact, record MCP backoff,
   and retry on a later tick. The failure is visible through the existing deploy_errors alarm path
   plus logs; it is not terminal state.

Rejected alternatives:

- Blue/green replacement self-heal: rejected after plan review because it starts a second MCP
  process under the same memory pressure that may have killed the first, collides with the
  retained dead container's name/port unless additional naming logic is added, and is unnecessary
  when the nginx include can remain valid.
- nginx multi-upstream/passive failover (`max_fails`/`fail_timeout` plus `backup`): rejected
  because open-source nginx can route around a failed primary only if a second live backend is
  already listed. The bounded MCP pool does not maintain a permanent spare, and passive failover
  would not start or readiness-check a replacement.
- Docker restart policy alone (`--restart always`): already present on MCP containers, but it is
  passive and has no operator-visible readiness proof tied to the `/mcp` upstream. The bug is that
  nginx can remain pinned while the process is dead or not ready; the autodeploy tick must make the
  restart/readiness outcome explicit and countable.
- Instance sizing/off-box gates: deferred to `inherited-americium-porpoise` / the bounded
  disk-ceiling and capacity campaign. Capacity may reduce recurrence, but it does not repair a
  dead served backend.

## Testing / verification plan

- RED test in `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` simulates nginx pointing at an
  exited managed MCP backend with no source change pending, and asserts one autodeploy tick runs
  `docker start` for that exact container, keeps the upstream byte-identical, emits
  `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL`, and returns success after readiness passes.
- RED companion test simulates `docker start` or readiness failure and asserts the container is not
  removed, upstream remains unchanged, existing `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR ... mcp-live-backend-down` is
  emitted, MCP backoff is recorded, and the next tick can retry.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`
  and full `make verify` before push.
- Live verification after merge: stop only the currently served MCP container with graceful Docker
  stop if needed, run one autodeploy tick, verify `/mcp` health recovers on the same upstream port,
  and confirm no persistent 502. No Terraform apply is required because the visible alarm path
  reuses existing `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`/deploy_errors wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The selected design is recorded with why alternatives were accepted/rejected.
- [ ] A reproduced or simulated MCP backend death under gate-like load recovers without a persistent nginx 502.
- [ ] The prevention is covered by tests through the relevant surface(s) and by an operator-visible metric/log/alarm.
- [ ] Any capacity/concurrency number used by the prevention cites measured data, including or linking the AC5 campaign split to `inherited-americium-porpoise`.


## RCA / design decision (2026-09-07)

This ticket is the remaining prevention gap after `witted-invisible-roan`: the current
blue/green deploy path refuses to delete a crashed live MCP backend, but it only logs
`mcp-live-backend-down` and waits for a source-changing redeploy or Docker restart. If the
container is exited/OOM-killed and Docker does not restart it promptly, nginx can stay pinned to
that dead single-server upstream and `/mcp` returns persistent 502.

Selected prevention: add an autodeploy self-heal path that runs on every tick before ordinary
source-change deploy decisions. When the live upstream port belongs to a managed MCP container
that is not running, autodeploy must:

1. keep the dead live container until after a replacement is promoted (no `rm -f` of the serving
   reference);
2. honor the existing MCP memory floor and two-port cap so healing cannot worsen the same
   memory-pressure class;
3. start a replacement from the currently deployed MCP image on the free blue/green port;
4. require the same `/health` readiness, store-readiness, startup-handshake, nginx-test, and
   nginx-reload gates as a normal MCP cutover;
5. atomically flip nginx to the replacement, then reap the old exited backend and emit countable
   journal markers (`AUTODEPLOY_MCP_SELF_HEAL` plus existing error markers on failure).

Rejected alternatives:

- nginx multi-upstream/failover: would hide a dead backend only when a second healthy backend
  already exists, but the existing design deliberately keeps a tiny bounded two-port pool and
  retires old never-idle backends; it does not guarantee spare live capacity after load.
- increasing instance size or only changing memory limits: AC4's measurement campaign is split
  to `inherited-americium-porpoise`; capacity may still be useful, but it does not repair a
  single-server nginx pointer after a process death.
- moving gates off-box: larger architecture change, not needed for the immediate persistent-502
  recurrence.

## Testing / verification plan

- RED test in `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` simulates nginx pointing at an
  exited managed MCP backend with no source change pending, and asserts the tick starts a
  replacement, flips upstream to it, emits a self-heal marker, and only then reaps the dead
  backend.
- Companion test covers low-memory self-heal refusal: no replacement starts, upstream remains
  unchanged, and the existing memory-abort marker is emitted.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`
  and full `make verify` before push.
- Live verification after merge: observe `/mcp/health` or container `/health`, and confirm no
  persistent 502 after intentionally abandoning scratch test changes; no Terraform alarm apply is
  required unless HCL changes emerge.

### Plan-review remediation notes

- Dead-live replacement must avoid the retained exited backend's identity. The self-heal path
  chooses a free port from ALL managed MCP containers (`docker ps -a`), so the dead live
  container's port stays reserved until after promotion; if no alternate blue/green port is free,
  the heal emits the existing retire-cap marker and backs off. Replacement container names include
  a `heal-<epoch>` suffix when the deployed SHA is unchanged, so Docker cannot collide with the
  retained dead container's name.
- Readiness/nginx failure disposition: a started replacement that fails `/health`, store readiness,
  startup handshake, `nginx -t`, or reload is removed if it never served, the dead live backend is
  retained for forensic safety, an existing MCP error marker is emitted, and the normal MCP
  backoff makes the next attempt retryable rather than terminal.
- Concurrency ownership: the existing autodeploy flock serializes the complete heal check/start/
  health/flip/reap sequence against both ordinary deploy ticks and another self-heal tick.
- Memory signal: readable below-floor memory aborts the heal before starting a second container;
  unreadable memory keeps the existing fail-open deploy behavior because a broken memory probe must
  not block recovery forever, but the path is visible in logs and still constrained by the two-port
  cap.
- Passive nginx `max_fails`/`fail_timeout` plus `backup` was considered and rejected: open-source
  nginx can avoid a failed primary only if the config already names another live upstream. The
  bounded MCP pool intentionally does not keep a permanent spare; passive checks would not start a
  replacement or restore serving capacity after the only listed backend dies.
